order: Fix continuous-integration failures on macOS and Windows that appeared following the structural sweep guard change. Git records canonical worktree paths, but a live checkout's own handle may be spelled through a symlink or a short alias path, so a lexical comparison inside the sweep's live-set exemption misses the match, and the sweep removes a live checkout mid-verification. The path-normalization function looks up real paths first, falling back to a lexical comparison only for paths that are already gone, and never for a path still on disk. Pin a regression using an aliased temporary-root reproducer, such as a junction or symlink, that must fail on every platform before the fix lands, and skip cleanly where links cannot be created. Confine the fix narrowly to the normalization function and the live-set comparison. The sweep's other classification logic stays exactly as it was.
claims: The live-set exemption's path comparison now looks up real paths, falling back lexically only for paths already gone, which fixes the macOS and Windows continuous-integration failures caused by a canonical-versus-aliased path mismatch. A regression was pinned using an aliased temporary-root reproducer, built from a junction or symlink, that fails on every platform absent the fix. The change spans 2 files in all, the verifier test suite and the checkout module, and no other part of the sweep was touched.
